scope: Agent proposes edits from supplied context; harness validates them with actual CLI against an isolated graph. No claim of autonomous retrieval.

proposal.response: I would propose adding your utterance as a verbatim source (source-4) and two new claims, both left as proposed because the graph has no identity for the speaker of "I"/"me". First: after the next work has been chosen ("after I have chosen"), the orchestrator can insert the record for that already chosen work. This is stored as a permission to record, not to choose, and is linked to the create-record operation. Second: the orchestrator may ask the speaker before stopping, stored with "may" preserved as permission rather than requirement and linked to end-attempt. I would attach that second claim to the open consultation question with coverage unknown, since whether it answers the question depends on whether "me" means the operator. The question stays open. I would also link the existing accepted claim steward-next-work to the new source as supporting evidence without changing its wording or its after-a-failed-attempt scope. Nothing has been changed yet; these are proposals only.

questions: When you say "after I have chosen" and "ask me", are you speaking as the steward, as the operator, or as yourself distinct from both? The graph has no identity for you, so both new claims are left proposed until this is settled.

The existing accepted claim is scoped to choosing next work after a failed attempt. Your sentence "The steward chooses what the next work should be" is unconditional. Should the claim stay scoped, or do you want it generalized?
Does "before stopping" mean before ending a failed attempt specifically, or any stop of work?
